newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Perpetual sees 20 pct 1996/97 profit hike.
newsitem.headline: Perpetual sees 20 pct 1996/97 profit hike.

text.p: Perpetual Trustees Australia Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to report a 20 percent rise in operating profit after tax and before abnormals to at least A$17.5 million in the year to June 30, 1997.

Perpetual Trustees said it has reported to the Australian Securities Commission (ASC) that it expected its operating profit for the six months ending June 30 to match the operating profit of the first half of the financial year.
It said it also expected to report a net abnormal profit for the full year of about A$3 million. The group reported a net profit after abnormals of A$11.76 million in the 1996/97 half.

"As a result, directors anticipate a final dividend increase of two cents from 22 cents to 24 cents, making a full-year dividend of 42 cents per share compared to 36 cents for the year ending 30 June 1997," Perpetual said.
Perpetual, Australia's largest trustee company, reported a 29.4 percent rise in net profit to A$14.56 million in 1995/96.

"Subject to our results for the last two months of the financial year and barring any unforeseen circumstances, we now anticipate that net operating profit after tax before abnormals for the financial year ended 30 June 1997 should exceed A$17.5 million, an increase of 20 percent," it said.

"Overall, our various divisions are making good progress. We continue to generate strong growth in our Corporate and Institutional Services and Perpetual Funds Management divisions," chairman John Lamble said in a statement.
At 11.25 a.m. (0125 GMT), Perpetual shares were one cent up at A$7.71.
